title: Fruit and Vegetable Scraps Could Boost Health — Study
paragraphs: Many of us throw away things like the skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables. But we could be discarding important health benefits along with these scraps!

A study published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition looked at 12 types of fruits and vegetables commonly eaten in the UK, including watermelon, broccoli and butternut squash.

Researchers examined the parts of each fruit or vegetable that are commonly thrown away. They found that in 10 out of 12, there are much higher levels of dietary fiber in the parts people don't usually consume compared with those they normally eat.

For example, watermelon rinds were found to contain around 2 grams of fiber per 100 grams, which is about the same as a slice of whole wheat bread. But the softer inside part of a watermelon has just 0.4 grams of dietary fiber per 100 grams.

Butternut squash skin and seeds offer a little over 9 grams of fiber per 100 grams — about one-third of the 30 grams the UK government recommends adults eat each day. That's much higher than the 2 grams of fiber per 100 grams found in the part of butternut squash usually eaten.
Broccoli was the exception — the stalks that people usually throw away have 28% less fiber than the florets on top of them, which are usually eaten.
Fiber is an important part of a healthy diet, improving digestion and reducing the risk of heart disease and some cancers. However, many people around the world don't get enough.
Using the often-discarded parts of fruit and vegetables could help — but people usually don't want to eat them.

So the researchers tried selling some recipes at foodservice outlets at King's College London. For nine weeks, students could buy things like watermelon salad that included the rind, or an African-style peanut stew with butternut squash skin and seeds.
These ended up representing around one-third of hot meal sales during those nine weeks — and in follow-up surveys, 77% of students said they'd likely choose them again!
